<SUMMARY>The week of June 12-19, 2026, was dominated by significant geopolitical and technological developments. The Group of Seven (G7) pledged to reduce its dependence on China for rare earth minerals, aiming to cap any single nation's supply at 60% by 2030, and established a critical minerals alliance. A Memorandum of Understanding between the United States and Iran was signed by President Donald Trump at Versailles to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with Pakistan and Qatar set to host the official ceremony in Switzerland. This deal has led to a forecast of a supply glut by the International Energy Agency and a fall in oil prices, while simultaneously accelerating the global energy transition with a solar boom in Southeast Asia and increased adoption of electric vehicles. In the technology sector, SK hynix shipped samples of its 12-layer HBM4E memory chips, and major investments were announced in AI infrastructure and semiconductor manufacturing, including Rumble's acquisition of 22,000 Nvidia chips and a 10-year advanced packaging deal between TSMC and Amkor in Arizona. President Trump also confirmed Apple's partnership with Intel to design and build chips in the US. Simultaneously, export controls intensified, with Taiwan moving to tighten AI chip export controls to China and the US restricting foreign access to Anthropic AI over suspected China-linked Korean Telecom. Critical discussions around the energy demands of AI infrastructure are also surfacing, highlighting a potential bottleneck for future growth.</SUMMARY>

<EWS>The US-Iran deal, despite easing immediate tensions, leaves key nuclear issues unresolved, which could lead to prolonged geopolitical uncertainty impacting global markets. The escalating energy demands of the AI boom pose an invisible energy crisis, threatening to derail expansion forecasts as electricity supply may not meet future needs. The US Department of Commerce restricted foreign access to Anthropic AI over suspected China-linked Korean Telecom, signaling intensified tech security concerns and potential for further AI model access restrictions. Huawei's continued comeback is testing the limits of existing US chip controls, highlighting ongoing challenges in tech sovereignty enforcement.</EWS>

<EXEC>
**Asia:**
SK hynix shipped samples of its 12-layer next-generation 'HBM4E' chips to major customers on June 17, achieving a maximum speed of 16Gbps per pin and utilizing Advanced MR-MUF to reduce heat resistance by 17%. Microsoft is building its AI model business in China, which highlights tension between cost-effective innovation and geopolitical tech security concerns. The G7 pledged on June 17 to cap China's rare earth dominance at 60% by 2030, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi hailed G7 unity on critical mineral supply chains. Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou's 2021 admissions about illegal business in Iran were ruled usable at criminal trial by a US judge. Taiwan's AI supply chain posted triple-digit gains in May as server makers and memory chips surged. Taiwan moved to tighten AI chip export controls to China on June 18. The U.S. blocked foreign access to Anthropic AI on June 16 over suspected China-linked Korean Telecom.

**Americas:**
Rumble acquired 22,000 Nvidia chips for infrastructure expansion, positioning itself as a formidable cloud competitor focused on privacy and sovereignty. Marvell Technology, a data infrastructure semiconductor provider, closed up 3.90% on June 17, following premarket comments from Nvidia's CEO and a new $2 billion AI chip alliance. The US awarded $500M to Nvidia-backed SandboxAQ on June 17 to discover new chipmaking materials, aimed at securing semiconductor supply chains and reducing reliance on foreign materials. Nokia announced a major expansion of its U.S. semiconductor advanced test and packaging operations in Pennsylvania on June 16 to bolster AI growth. TSMC and Amkor signed a 10-year Arizona packaging deal on June 16, aiming to complete the U.S. chip supply chain. President Donald Trump confirmed on June 18 that Apple will partner with Intel to design and build chips in the US. The invisible energy crisis is threatening to derail the AI boom, as electricity supply is projected to be insufficient for future AI power needs. PMET advanced its on-site lithium refining strategy through a technology collaboration MOU with Mitsui and MWCC in Montreal on June 17, leveraging Quebec’s low-cost renewable hydroelectricity.

**Africa:**
Public anger is mounting in Kenya as critics accuse Nairobi of capitulating to U.S. interests by cozying up to President Trump.

**Europe:**
French President Emmanuel Macron stated on June 17 that he expects progress in coming weeks on broadening access to leading U.S. AI models like Anthropic's Mythos, following G7 leaders' pledge for closer coordination on AI risks and opportunities. The European cybersecurity agency Enisa will hold a meeting with U.S. artificial intelligence company Anthropic in San Francisco on June 17. Infineon is set to open a new fab in Germany as part of a sovereignty push. Intel began production of its anticipated 18A-P chips, driven by AI demand. Huawei's big comeback is testing the limits of US chip controls. Tesco moved 40,000 server workloads off VMware on June 17 amid a Broadcom lawsuit seeking over £100M, a move that could set a precedent for enterprise IT spending.

**Oceania:**
PsiQuantum broke ground in Moreton Bay, Queensland, on June 17 for what it states will be the world’s first utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer, planning to house tens of thousands of photonic quantum chips.</EXEC>

<LITHO>

**Americas:**
Nokia announced a major expansion of its U.S. semiconductor advanced test and packaging operations in Pennsylvania on June 16, aimed at bolstering AI growth. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) and Amkor signed a 10-year advanced packaging deal in Arizona on June 16, which aims to complete the U.S. chip supply chain. President Donald Trump confirmed on June 18 that Apple will partner with Intel to design and build chips in the US, providing a significant endorsement for Intel's foundry efforts. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan made the decision to become CEO after being convinced by his wife and others to "save Intel".

**Europe:**
Intel's fab roadmap includes Ireland for its 14A process node, with decisions on what gets built next expected this year. Infineon is set to open a fab in Germany as part of a sovereignty push. Samsung Semiconductor detailed advancements "From GAA to 3D Stacked FET", expanding the transistor into the third dimension. An Nvidia-backed optics vendor aims to boost wafer output by 4x to meet AI interconnect demand.</LITHO>

<REE>
**Asia:**
The G7 pledged on June 17 to ensure no single nation supplies more than 60% of rare earth minerals by 2030, directly targeting China's dominance. Rare earth stocks experienced a spike after this G7 plan was unveiled. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi highlighted G7 unity on critical mineral supply chains.

**Africa:**
The race for East Africa’s critical minerals is upending regional conservation efforts. A dispute concerning DR Congo and Belgium’s colonial-era geological maps has been explained.

**Europe:**
The G7 established a critical minerals alliance and crisis platform to counter China's dependency, with the summit taking place in France on June 17. The alliance aims to reshape global supply chains and reduce geopolitical risks.</REE>

<GEO>
**Asia:**
Calbee's black-and-white potato chips appeared on Tokyo store shelves on June 17, reflecting the company's response to concerns over the stability of printing ink supplies derived from naphtha as tensions in the Middle East disrupt supply. The U.S. blocked foreign access to Anthropic AI on June 16 over suspected China-linked Korean Telecom.

**Americas:**
The US renaming Indo-Pacific Command to Pacific Command is signaling a strategic shift and raising concerns among experts about India’s role in the Quad and regional security.

**Africa:**
Public anger is mounting in Kenya as critics accuse Nairobi of capitulating to U.S. interests over those of Kenyan citizens.

**Europe:**
Tesco is in a legal battle with Broadcom, moving 40,000 server workloads off VMware amid a lawsuit seeking over £100M, a move that could set a precedent affecting enterprise IT spending. Cancer-linked 'forever chemicals' (PFAS) were discovered in every food item analyzed from Tesco own-brand fish, dairy, and meat products, described as an "alarming" revelation.</GEO>

<MILITARY>
**Oceania:**
DARPA launched a military battery program on June 16 targeting a 10x energy boost. Robot soldiers are predicted to take over the battlefield. The US introduced a new artillery shell that can fly 74 miles and change course mid-flight.

**Europe:**
Europe's new cruise missile can strike targets over 1,000 km away. Germany moved two ships to Djibouti on June 18, eyeing a multinational Hormuz mission for the summer.</MILITARY>

<CONCLUSION>The G7's commitment to cap China's rare earth dominance at 60% by 2030 and establish a critical minerals alliance signifies a strategic pivot towards supply chain diversification and geopolitical risk reduction. The US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding, signed by President Donald Trump at Versailles, has immediately impacted global energy markets, leading to a forecast of an oil supply glut and falling prices, while concurrently accelerating the global energy transition with a solar boom in Southeast Asia and a boost for electric vehicles. The intense demand for AI chips is driving significant investments in advanced packaging and new material discovery, notably with the TSMC/Amkor Arizona deal and the US grant to SandboxAQ, but faces looming challenges regarding energy infrastructure and geopolitical controls, as evidenced by Taiwan's new AI chip export controls to China and US restrictions on Anthropic AI access. These interconnected developments underscore a global landscape increasingly defined by technological competition, energy security, and the pursuit of supply chain resilience.</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>Gujarat SEZ exports reached Rs 3,00,793 crore in FY26, marking a 67% increase since 2014-15 and representing 21% of India’s total SEZ exports, accompanied by rising jobs, investment, and new semiconductor SEZs. India's significant gold imports, exceeding 800 tonnes in 2024 while producing only 2 tonnes, highlight a missed opportunity for domestic production and exploration. NITI Aayog urges India's AI self-reliance after recent US export controls. Relations between India and the US are complicated by the killing of Indian sailors by the U.S. military. The US decision to rename Indo-Pacific Command to Pacific Command raises concerns about India’s role in the Quad and regional security.</INDIA>

<WEST_ASIA>President Donald Trump signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Iran in Versailles on June 17, aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Pakistan and Qatar are scheduled to host the Iran-US agreement ceremony in Switzerland on June 19. The US-Iran MoU is anticipated to stabilize Middle Eastern geopolitics and global energy markets, although sanctions on Iranian digital assets remain unchanged. However, key nuclear issues remain unresolved in the deal, which could lead to prolonged geopolitical uncertainty and raises a $300B question. The Pentagon AI chief confirmed on June 17 that Musk’s Grok AI tool was used to guide US strikes and deploy thousands of missiles at Iran. The US-Iran war is significantly affecting the global energy transition, identifying EVs and US oil as winners, and spurring a solar boom in Southeast Asia. Europe is exploring energy security alternatives following the turmoil from the Iran war. The International Energy Agency forecasts a supply glut next year, and oil prices fell on June 18 after the US-Iran deal. South Korea’s economy accelerated on June 17 despite the Middle East energy shock. The US-Iran pact is reshaping Middle East energy maps.</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The coming period will likely see continued aggressive strategies by nations to secure technological sovereignty and diversify critical supply chains, particularly in semiconductors and rare earth minerals, given the G7's explicit targets and ongoing export control measures. The US-Iran agreement is poised to fundamentally alter global energy dynamics, shifting focus towards alternative energy sources and potentially impacting oil market stability for the long term. The burgeoning AI industry, while driving unprecedented innovation and investment, must contend with significant energy infrastructure challenges, which could become a limiting factor for its growth and necessitate strategic national interventions. Further scrutiny on the ethical and military applications of advanced AI models, as demonstrated by the reported use of Grok AI in US strikes, will be a central theme in international security discussions.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
